derivation_exp_plus_iwt.step_3_fixed_wall: set T_bnd=0, v_n=0 and v0_t=0; retain the tangential pressure Laplacian and isothermal thermal-compliance terms
derivation_exp_plus_iwt.step_5_weak_residual: after placing the pressure-dependent wall terms on the left and applying surface Green integration to Delta_t(p), add integral_Gamma 2*pi*r*[c_v*grad_t(p).grad_t(q)+c_t*p*q] ds

step_6_coefficients.axisymmetric_weight: 2*pi*r is assembled in boundary matrices, not hidden in scalar coefficients

derivation_exp_plus_iwt.step_7_passivity: for exp(+i omega t), Im(c_v)>=0 and Im(c_t)>=0; P_visc=Im(c_v)*(p^H K_t p)/(2*omega), P_thermal=Im(c_t)*(p^H M_b p)/(2*omega), so both are nonnegative for positive-semidefinite axisymmetric boundary matrices
derivation_exp_plus_iwt.zero_loss: loss_scale=0 gives exactly zero coefficients and zero BLI dissipation

implementation.nra_separation: circular reference is an independent Bessel solution and never calls the repository parallel-slit NRA

case_c_applicability.corner_risk: BLI applies to smooth wall segments; unresolved sharp-corner neighborhoods remain a local full-TV risk rather than being assigned zero curvature

circular_duct_reference.outgoing_convention: exp(-i*k*z), so passive attenuation requires Im(k)<=0 and attenuation=-Im(k)>=0
circular_duct_reference.wide_limit: relative exact/asymptotic error decreases as radius/boundary-layer thickness increases
circular_duct_reference.parameter_trends: increased mu increases viscous coefficient and circular attenuation; increased kappa increases thermal coefficient and circular attenuation
